subject: CAIQ: control ambiguity and evidence escrow plan
messages:
From: Priya Sharma <psharma@argentfinancial.com>
To: mateo_alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: CAIQ follow-up + ambiguity on CC-4 mapping

Hi Mateo —

Thanks again for the workshop this morning. Our audit team ran through the draft CAIQ you shared and flagged a couple of ambiguous control mappings that we need clarified before we hand the packet to our external auditors.

Two quick examples:
- CC-4.2 (key rotation) — your crosswalk refers to both "KMS rotation policy" and "customer-managed HSM" as evidence. Our auditors want a deterministic path: which artifact proves automated rotation vs a manual process?
- CC-7.1 (runtime isolation) — the comment in cell F12 implies a tenant-level keystore; is that a logical separation in the control narrative or an enforced physical boundary?

I've attached the annotated CAIQ PDF with inline notes and a small workbook summarizing the gaps. Can we get a short plan for what artifacts you'll deliver and who owns each item?

Michael from Skylark (cc'd) will use this to scope his review.

Best,
Priya Sharma
Director, IT Assurance
Argent Financial

Attachments: Argent-CAIQ-Questions-20261101.pdf (PDF, 4 pages)
             redline_control_map_v1.xlsx (Excel, 1 sheet)

From: mateo_alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <psharma@argentfinancial.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CAIQ follow-up + ambiguity on CC-4 mapping

Hi Priya —

Appreciate the detailed notes and the workbook, this is helpful. Short answers up front:
- CC-4.2 (key rotation): Redwood maintains an automated rotation policy for platform keys (KMS). For customer-managed keys/HSMs we provide attestations and rotation runbooks — they are different evidence types. We'll mark the crosswalk to show the primary artifact per scope (automated rotation log for platform keys; key-rotation-runbook + rotation evidence for HSM).
- CC-7.1 (runtime isolation): currently this is a logical isolation enforced by tenant-aware routing and per-tenant keystore namespaces. We will not claim physical separation unless you purchase the Dedicated offering; I'll note the difference in the narrative.

Action plan proposal (high level):
1) Kimberly — take ownership of CC-4.2 artifacts and produce a short artifact index (target: 2026-11-04).
2) Marissa — capture the runtime isolation narrative and pull example log lines demonstrating tenant namespace enforcement (target: 2026-11-05).
3) Mateo — assemble the escrow plan for evidence delivery and give Priya a single archive link + evidence manifest by 2026-11-06.

I'll follow up with the manifest and a Drive link once we have the artifacts staged. If that timeline is tight for Skylark, let us know and we can prioritize.

Thanks —
Mateo Alvarez
Technical Program Manager, Trust & Security
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 11:07:00 -0800

Forwarding my notes and a short sample extraction I ran this morning.

On the tenant isolation question — I pulled three anonymized runtime traces that show tenant_id headers and the keystore namespace resolution from our staging cluster. These will need redaction but should satisfy the "evidence of enforcement" requirement.

Attached: runtime_traces_sample.txt (text, 3 examples)

Kimberly — I'm dropping the CC-4 artifact list into the shared Drive folder under /Argent/Evidence-Delivery. Please add any additional files and mark one primary artifact per control in column B of the redline_control_map_v1.xlsx.

Marissa
